amendments.because: A client worker repeatedly edited forge.toml temporarily mid-run to make forge test run an extra suite (2026-10-09)
amendments.done_when: The commit hook refuses a commit inside a worker run that changes forge.toml unless the item's Done-when names forge.toml (settings fixes and release bumps keep working), saying plainly that settings change in their own fix; the worker brief says workers never edit forge.toml and should report a needed settings change in their last message instead; command tests cover a refused worker commit, an allowed settings fix, and a coordinator commit outside a worker run, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

done_when: The commit hook refuses a commit inside a worker run that changes forge.toml unless the item's Done-when names forge.toml (settings fixes and release bumps keep working), saying plainly that settings change in their own fix; the worker brief says workers never edit forge.toml, not even temporarily, and that to run an extra suite they run its command directly alongside forge test; when a worker round ends with forge.toml changed but uncommitted, Forge restores it from the branch and says so in the round's hand-back, unless the Done-when names forge.toml; command tests cover a refused worker commit, an allowed settings fix, a coordinator commit outside a worker run, and a round that leaves forge.toml edited, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: `FORGE_WORKER` also marks coordinator-launched Git commands: `src/forge/repo.py:120` unconditionally sets it in `run()`. Consequently, this guard breaks `forge upgrade`: `src/forge/upgrade.py:89` creates a Done-when without `forge.toml`, and its commit at line 162 inherits the marker and is refused after sync installs the new hook. The same problem affects coordinator merge recovery at `src/forge/close.py:463` when incoming settings changes are staged. These operations occur outside worker rounds. Distinguish actual worker commits from coordinator-generated commits. The supplied coordinator test uses raw `subprocess.run`, so it passes without exercising this failure.
findings.title: Not done: Keep coordinator commits and release upgrades working outside worker runs

why: Workers sometimes edit forge.toml while building an unrelated task or fix (a client worker added a command to fast_test because a note mentioned it; earlier a worker moved the version pin), though forge.toml is the coordinator's to change, through a settings fix the owner asked for (reported by a client session, 2026-10-09)
